Synopsis:
Alcoa's CFO argues that even a halving of the 50% U.S. tariff on Canadian aluminum would not meaningfully reduce the elevated U.S. Midwest aluminum premium (~$1.09/lb), as the U.S. requires ~4Mt/year of imports while Canada can only supply ~3Mt. The residual 1Mt gap must be sourced elsewhere, keeping the premium structurally elevated. Broader tariff relief covering other partners (EU, Japan, South Korea) would risk eroding the premium entirely. Alcoa is absorbing >$1B in tariff costs on its ~900Kt Canadian output but is fully compensated — and then some — via the high Midwest premium. Middle East supply disruptions are tightening global aluminum availability, boosting demand for Alcoa's supply, with its 2026 order book nearly fully sold out.
